sutta: Now we come to 12.31. On occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Savatthi. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sariputta thus, "Sariputta, in the questions of Ajita in the Parayana, it is said, 'Those who have comprehended the Dhamma and the manyfold trainees here asked about their way of conduct being discreet. Tell me, dear sir, how should the meaning of this stated in brief be understood in detail?'" Let's stop here for a moment. This Parayana is a chapter from the Sutta Nipata. It is a book in the Khuddaka Nikaya, the last Nikaya. But the Sutta Nipata is considered one of the old books. Uh one of the original uh teachings of the Buddha. So here the Buddha is asking the Venerable Sariputta in this particular sutta. Concerning the questions of Ajita, there is a verse there that says, "Those who have comprehended the Dhamma and the manyfold trainees here asked about their way of conduct being discreet. Tell me, dear sir, how the Buddha is asking him, how do you explain this? Uh And this was said, the Venerable Sariputta was silent. The second time and the third time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sariputta thus, "Uh in the same way now, Sariputta, in the questions of Ajita in the Parayana, it is said, etc. etc. How should the meaning of this stated in brief be understood in detail? The second time and the third time the Venerable Sariputta was silent." So the Venerable Sariputta was not sure how to answer. So he kept quiet. Then the Buddha said, "Sariputta, do you see this has come to be? Sariputta, do you see this has come to be?" So the Buddha prompted him. And he said, "Venerable sir, one sees it one sees as it really is with correct wisdom. This has come to be. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom, this has come to be. One is practicing for the purpose of revulsion towards what has come to be, for its fading away and cessation. One sees as it as it really is with correct wisdom. Its origination occurs with that as nutriment. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom, its origination occurs with that as nutriment. One is practicing for the purpose of revulsion towards its origination through nutriment, for its fading away and cessation. One sees as it really is with correct wisdom with the cessation of that nutriment. What has come to be is subject to cessation. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom with the cessation of that nutriment. What has come to be is subject to cessation. One is practicing for the purpose of revulsion towards what is subject to cessation, for its fading away and cessation. It's in such a way that one is a trainee. And how, Venerable sir, has one comprehended the Dhamma? Venerable sir, one sees as it really is with correct wisdom. This has come to be. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom, this has come to be through revulsion towards what has come to be, through its fading away and cessation. One is liberated by non-clinging. One sees as it really is with correct wisdom. Its origination occurs with that as nutriment. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom, its origination occurs with that as nutriment through revulsion towards its origination through nutriment, through its fading away and cessation. One is liberated by non-clinging. One sees as it really is with correct wisdom with the with the cessation of that nutriment. What has come to be is subject to cessation. Having seen as it really is with correct wisdom with the cessation of that nutriment. What has come to be is subject to cessation through revulsion towards what is subject to cessation, through its fading away and cessation. One is liberated by non-clinging. It is it is in such a way that one has comprehended the Dhamma. Thus, Venerable sir, when it is said in the questions of Ajita in the Parayana, "Those who have comprehended the Dhamma and the manyfold trainees here asked about their way of conduct being discreet. Tell me, dear sir, it is in such a way that I understand in detail the meaning of this that was stated in brief." "Good, good, Sariputta." And the Buddha repeats the entire statement of the Venerable Sariputta. "It is in such a way that the meaning of this stated in brief should be understood in detail. That's the end of the sutra. So here you see the Buddha asked him a question after Venerable Sariputta. Although he is the disciple with the highest wisdom, he also found it a bit difficult to answer. He didn't know exactly what the Buddha wanted him to say. So when the Buddha prompted him by saying uh Sariputta, do you see this has come to be? And then he he he caught it. He caught the clue. So he answered the Buddha. First he explained about the the trainee. That means the the trainee here refers to the Pali word Sekha. Sekha is one who is still training. Uh and it means the Aryans below the Arahan. There are eight types of Aryans, noble ones, uh uh holy persons. The lowest is the first path. And then that first path after some time will automatically become the first fruit. Then the second path attain and then the second fruit, third path attain, third fruit, and fourth path attain and fourth fruit. These are the eight types of holy men, Aryans. Out of these eight, only the Arahan, the fourth fruit person, or the Buddha, the Buddha and Arahan are both uh fourth fruit attainers. Only the the fourth fruit attainer has completed his work. So he's called Asekha. Uh one who does not need to train anymore. Whereas the other seven are called Sekha, trainees. So here the Venerable Sariputta is explaining uh what what is the state of the train trainee. The Venerable Sariputta says a trainee, he will he will see with wisdom this has come to be. Something that exists has come into existence. And then it originates because of certain conditions which we call nutriment. Nutriment is a condition for that thing to come into existence. And then he also sees with the cessation of that nutriment uh what has come to be is subject to cessation. Then having seen this, is practicing for the purpose of revulsion towards what is subject to cessation. For example, the things in the world, for example, somebody that you love is subject to cessation, subject to aging, sickening, and dying. So you you you see that this person that you love because it's subject to cessation and it is dependent on certain conditions to keep it alive. And so the trainee the is practicing for the purpose of revulsion towards what is subject to cessation. This that we cling to, if we see that it's impermanent, that it's subject to cessation, then if you are practicing for the purpose of revulsion, disenchantment towards this that we we attach to, then one is a trainee. That means you you you are practicing to let go. Practice to let go. You are a trainee, one who has seen but has not finished the work. Whereas the Arahan, he sees the same thing but he has revulsion. He already has achieved revulsion towards what has come to be, revulsion towards its origination to nutriment, and so on. Uh to revulsion towards what is subject to cessation. Through its fading away and cessation, one is liberated by non-clinging. This in such a way that one has comprehended the Dhamma. So one who has comprehended the Dhamma fully, one who has finished his work, he has total revulsion towards all that is subject to cessation, all the things in the world being impermanent. If we cling to it, we will suffer. So the Arahan, he has totally become disenchanted with everything in the world and he lets go. So then he has comprehended the Dhamma. That's the difference. One is practicing towards that state, whereas the other one has already achieved revulsion.
